description: List observatories whose telescope share is above the average share, ordered by how far above average they are. Return exactly 10 rows, breaking any tie at the cutoff arbitrarily.

c.request: For each observatory station, count its telescopes and work out its share of all telescopes (its count divided by the total number of telescopes). Which are the top 10 observatories whose share is above the average share across observatories, ranked by how far above average they are? Show the `observstation`, the telescope count, the share, and the share minus the average share, unrounded, from the biggest gap to the smallest. List observatories whose telescope share is above the average share, ordered by how far above average they are. Return exactly 10 rows, breaking any tie at the cutoff arbitrarily.
c.sql: WITH station_counts AS (SELECT o.observstation, COUNT(t.telescregistry) AS telescope_count FROM observatories AS o LEFT JOIN telescopes AS t ON t.observstation = o.observstation GROUP BY o.observstation), station_shares AS (SELECT observstation, telescope_count, 1.0 * telescope_count / SUM(telescope_count) OVER () AS share FROM station_counts), compared AS (SELECT observstation, telescope_count, share, share - AVG(share) OVER () AS share_above_average FROM station_shares) SELECT observstation, telescope_count, share, share_above_average FROM compared WHERE share_above_average > 0 ORDER BY share_above_average DESC LIMIT 10;

a.request: For each observatory station, count its telescopes and work out its share of all telescopes (its count divided by the total number of telescopes). Among observatories whose share is above the average share across all observatories, list the `observstation`, the telescope count, the share, and how far the share is above the average (share minus average share), with no rounding. Sort by that difference from largest to smallest and return exactly the first 10 rows; if observatories are tied at the 10th place, just pick any of them to fill the 10 rows.
a.sql: WITH station_counts AS (SELECT o.observstation, COUNT(t.telescregistry) AS telescope_count FROM observatories AS o LEFT JOIN telescopes AS t ON t.observstation = o.observstation GROUP BY o.observstation), shares AS (SELECT observstation, telescope_count, 1.0 * telescope_count / NULLIF(SUM(telescope_count) OVER (), 0) AS share FROM station_counts), ranked AS (SELECT observstation, telescope_count, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS average_share FROM shares) SELECT observstation, telescope_count, share, share - average_share AS difference_above_average FROM ranked WHERE share > average_share ORDER BY difference_above_average DESC LIMIT 10;

b.request: For each observatory station, count its telescopes, divide that count by the total number of telescopes, and subtract the average telescope share across observatories; return the 10 stations with shares above that average, showing `observstation`, telescope count, share, and unrounded difference, ordered by difference descending, with ties at the cutoff broken arbitrarily
b.sql: WITH station_counts AS (SELECT o.observstation, COUNT(t.telescregistry) AS telescope_count FROM observatories AS o LEFT JOIN telescopes AS t ON t.observstation = o.observstation GROUP BY o.observstation), station_shares AS (SELECT observstation, telescope_count, 1.0 * telescope_count / NULLIF(SUM(telescope_count) OVER (), 0) AS share FROM station_counts), compared AS (SELECT observstation, telescope_count, share, share - AVG(share) OVER () AS difference FROM station_shares) SELECT observstation, telescope_count, share, difference FROM compared WHERE difference > 0 ORDER BY difference DESC LIMIT 10

d.request: For each observatory station, count its telescopes and calculate its share of all telescopes as its count divided by the total telescope count. List the 10 observatories whose share exceeds the average share across observatories, ordered by share minus average share from largest to smallest. Return `observstation`, telescope count, share, and share minus average share, all unrounded. Break any tie at the cutoff arbitrarily.
d.sql: WITH station_counts AS (SELECT o.observstation, COUNT(t.telescregistry) AS telescope_count FROM observatories AS o LEFT JOIN telescopes AS t ON t.observstation = o.observstation GROUP BY o.observstation), shares AS (SELECT observstation, telescope_count, 1.0 * telescope_count / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM telescopes) AS share FROM station_counts), average_share AS (SELECT AVG(share) AS value FROM shares) SELECT s.observstation, s.telescope_count, s.share, s.share - a.value AS share_minus_average_share FROM shares AS s CROSS JOIN average_share AS a WHERE s.share > a.value ORDER BY share_minus_average_share DESC LIMIT 10;
